title: Aliens
build: US Activision disk, 'Aliens [Activision].d64', a cracked copy: a Remember cracktro and trainer (22 KB BASIC file at $0801) in front of ten packed game files A0-A9

Starts the briefing: interrupts off, sprites off, the raster call to intro_raster ($80C2), and the VIC-II set from the list after the call.
vic_inline_writes's list, register and value: $D011=$2B, $D012=$10, $D016=$08, $D018=$79, $D019=$FF, $D01A=$81, $D020=$00, $D021=$0B, $D015=$00; $FF ends it.
Inside the list: its first value, $2B.
VIC-II bank 1, text to the bitmap $6000 and screen $5C00, page 6 and the bitmap cleared, the screen's colours set to $0B, the engine's objects off, and the screen on.

The four pages of text, one after another: each is printed with the 8-pixel font (print) from brief_page_ptrs and waits for RETURN; after the fourth ($0600 = 4) the scene on the Sulaco begins (scene_start).
The four pages' addresses: $80C6, $8291, $8492 and $86C8.
brief_page_ptrs read from its second byte: the high bytes.
The raster call while the pages show: frame_tick only.
"CONFERENCE ROOM - GATEWAY STATION. RIPLEY FACES A BOARD OF INQUIRY." Van Leuwen reads the lifeboat's flight recorder.
More of page 1; the trainer pokes $8139, $813A and $813B when it loads level 6.
The second of level 6's pokes into page 1.
The third of level 6's pokes into page 1.
More of page 1; the trainer pokes $8178 for level 4.
The ECA representative: "You found something which has never been reported once from over three hundred surveyed worlds."
More of page 2; the trainer pokes $839C, $839D and $839E for level 1.
Level 1's second poke into page 2.
More of page 2, where level 1's third poke lands.
Van Leuwen: "It is the finding of this board that Officer Ripley has acted with questionable judgment...", and the talk of the colonists on LV-426.
"SEVERAL WEEKS LATER... RIPLEY'S APARTMENT - GATEWAY STATION." Carter Burke and Lieutenant Gorman at Ripley's door: "They've lost contact with the colony on LV-426..."
More of page 4; the trainer pokes $8798 for level 5.
More of page 4; the trainer pokes $881B and $8854 for level 3.
More of page 4; the trainer pokes $8854 for level 3.
The scene on the Sulaco: the bitmap off, the music stopped ($04B5 = $FF), CIA 1's interrupts off, the raster call to scene_raster ($88E9), and the VIC-II set from the list after the call.
VIC-II bank 1, page 6 cleared, the engine's objects off, the picture unpacked (scene_unpack), the first balloon printed with the wide font, the screen on, and sfx_drone.
Inside the LDA: the trainer pokes $88A9, $88AC and $88B5 when it loads level 6, whose own code lies here then.
Inside the STA: the trainer pokes $88AC for level 6.
Inside the JSR: the trainer pokes $88B5 for level 6.
start_effect with sfx_drone ($39D0).
start_effect's argument: $39D0 (sfx_drone).
On to the wait for RETURN.
Each balloon in turn from balloon_ptrs, printed with the wide font (print_wide), then a wait for RETURN; after the fourteenth ($0601 = 14) the equipment identification begins (equip_start).
Waits for RETURN, then the next balloon.

The raster call during the scene: level_frame, then sprite 0 as the balloon's tail pointing at the speaker, from the tables by balloon number $0601: its frame (balloon_tail), x (balloon_x), and whether it is stretched across and down; black, with light grey and dark grey for its multicolours, at y $70.
The tail's sprite frame for each of the 14 balloons: 1 or 2, pointing one way or the other.
The tail's x for each balloon: $F0, $78, $B0 or $B4, by speaker.
Whether the tail is stretched across ($D01D) for each balloon.
Whether it is stretched down ($D017) for each balloon.
Fourteen more bytes (6 to $20) that no code reads as a table: only $895C is read, as balloon_tall's entry 14 in the last frame before the scene ends. What they were for is unknown.
Unpacks the scene's picture (scene_picture).
unpack_inline's arguments: the packed picture at $9810, 5,325 bytes long.
The scene picture's packed length, $14CD, then the RTS.
Back from unpacking the scene.
The 14 balloons' addresses, $898E to $8EB2.
balloon_ptrs from its second byte: the high bytes.
The first balloon: "At ease. I'm sorry we didn't have time to brief you before we left Gateway, but..."
"Sir?"
"Yes, Hicks?"
"Hudson, sir. He's Hicks."
Inside balloon 4; the trainer pokes $8A89 for level 2.
"What's the question?"
"Is this going to be a stand-up fight, sir, or just another bug hunt?"
"All we know is that there's still no contact with the colony and that a xenomorph may be involved."
Inside balloon 7; the trainer pokes $8B64 for level 5.
"It's a bug hunt."
"I'll tell you what I know. One of our crew members was brought back with this thing on his face..."
"It must have laid something inside him... down his throat."
"Look, man, I only need to know one thing..."
"Where they are!"
"I hope you're right. I really do."
Inside balloon 13; the trainer pokes $8E8E for level 4.
"I want DCS and tactical database assimilation by 0830. Ordnance loading, weapons strip..."
Inside balloon 14; the trainer pokes $8EB8 for level 4.
Inside balloon 14; the trainer pokes $8F66 for level 2.
The equipment identification: the bitmap off, the raster call to equip_raster ($90CD), and the VIC-II set from the list after the call.
Page 6 cleared, the picture of the seven pieces unpacked (equip_unpack), the glove at x $30, y $40, the engine's objects off, VIC-II bank 1, the bitmap on.

For each state $0602 in turn: its text from equip_texts printed with the wide font (print_list's entry at $239A), a $88 in the text clearing the text area (equip_clear_text) and going on; then the state's handler from equip_handlers.
A JSR back to the print loop at $8FE3 that nothing reaches.
The state's handler, written into the JMP at $9004.
The handler's address, low byte (written here).
Its high byte.

The handler of each state: 0 the countdown, on to state 1 ($901D); 1 to 7 the seven pieces, each waiting for fire over the right one ($9023); 8 the end ($90A7); 9 improper ($9088); 10 confirmed ($9096).
equip_handlers from its second byte: the high bytes.
State 0 done: on to the first piece.
Inside the INC: the low byte of $0602.

Waits for fire ($0223 bit 4), then tests the glove's place ($0604, $0605) against the piece's box in equip_boxes. Inside it: sfx_chord and state 10, confirmed. Outside: sfx_chord2 and state 9, improper. Either way the piece's state is kept in $0608.
Inside the STA: the trainer pokes $9045 when it loads level 5, whose own code lies here then.
start_effect's argument: $3958, sfx_chord, for a piece named right.
Keeps the piece in $0608 and goes to state 10, confirmed.
start_effect's argument: $3994, sfx_chord2, for a wrong piece.
Keeps the piece in $0608 and goes to state 9, improper.
State 9, after "IMPROPER IDENTIFICATION": back to the same piece, with sfx_drone.
start_effect's argument: $39D0, sfx_drone, after a wrong answer.
Back to the loop.
State 10, after "EQUIPMENT VERIFICATION CONFIRMED": on to the next piece, with sfx_drone.
start_effect's argument: $39D0, sfx_drone, after a right answer.
Back to the loop, at the next piece.
State 8: waits for RETURN and ends the stage (stage_complete); level 1 follows.

Four bytes for each state: the left, top, right and bottom of the piece's box in the glove's units (x before doubling, sprite y), the glove inside when left and top or more and below right and bottom. States 1 to 7: pistol, flame thrower, locator band, smart-gun, pulse rifle, motion tracker and camera.
equip_boxes from its second byte: the tops.
equip_boxes from its third byte: the right edges.
equip_boxes from its fourth byte: the bottoms, read as the box's limit below.
A TAX before equip_raster that nothing reaches.

The raster call during the identification: level_frame, sprites 0-2 on, the glove's frames 3 and 4 (its finger up, and the outline) or 5 and 6 with fire held (the finger down), then the glove moved (glove_move).
Unpacks the picture of the seven pieces (equip_picture).
Inside the JSR: unpack_inline's high byte.
unpack_inline's arguments: the packed picture at $9329, 1,255 bytes long.
The equipment picture's packed length, $04E7.
Back from unpacking.
The joystick ($0222) moves the glove two lines a frame up and down (y $39 to $A6) and one step across (x $20 to $9B); sprites 0 and 1 at x, sprite 2, its outline, three right and three down.
Clears the text area of the bitmap, $72C0-$7F40.
The text for each state: the countdown, the seven pieces' names, the end, improper and confirmed; entries 11 to 13 are all $9329, past the texts.
equip_texts from its second byte: the high bytes.
"EQUIPMENT IDENTIFICATION", then "IN 05-" down to "IN 01-", each followed by $80, a wait of 63 frames.
Part of the countdown; the trainer pokes $91DE for level 5.
"PISTOL:", after $88, which clears the text area.
"FLAME THROWER:".
"LOCATOR BAND:".
"SMART-GUN:".
"M-41A 10MM PULSE RIFLE W/ 30MM GRENADE LAUNCHER:".
"MOTION TRACKER:".
"IMAGE-INTENSIFIED IR VIDEO CAMERA W/ BIO-MONITOR TRANSCEIVER:".
Inside text 7; the trainer pokes $9299 for level 5.
"IDENTIFICATION SEQUENCE COMPLETE", then "(PRESS RETURN TO CONTINUE)".
"IMPROPER IDENTIFICATION", then a wait.
"EQUIPMENT VERIFICATION CONFIRMED", then a wait.
The seven pieces of equipment on grey, packed (1,255 bytes, to $980F).
The last of the equipment picture.
The marines in the Sulaco's hold, packed (5,325 bytes, to $ACDC).
The scene's picture, packed, continued.
The scene's picture, packed, across $A000 (BASIC's ROM, switched out).
The scene's picture, packed, further on.
The scene's picture, packed, its later part.
The scene's picture, packed, near its end.
The last of the scene's picture, packed.
Zero bytes to the end of the page.
